messages:
sara: heads up — I'm seeing a burst of opaque NVMe IO errors on scratch nodes in us-west1 correlated with a spike in GPU attach failures. provisioning queues are backing up.

mike: ugh. any iostats or dmesg snippets?

sara: pasted a quick iostat run from gnode-uw1-045:```
Linux 5.10.0-... (gnode-uw1-045) 
Device            r/s    w/s  rkB/s  wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s  r_await  w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         12.00  85.00  120.0  680.0    0.00    1.00    4.20    12.50  1.70  92.30
```
This coincides with dozens of ephemeral-cleaner workers running and a flood of small deletes.

jamal: SMART shows rising reallocated sectors on a few drives (threshold approaching). not full SMART failure yet but suspicious.

elaine: are we seeing actual blocks marked bad or just timeouts?

sara: mostly timeouts and opaque I/O errors in kernel logs:```
[ 1234.567890] nvme nvme0: I/O 0x7ff failed: status=0x8 - timeout
[ 1234.567899] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567
```

oncall-maya: infra-bot flagged degraded-iops-us-west1 alert at 1739998860. linking here. @sara @mike

infra-bot: ALERT degraded-iops-us-west1 - metric:local_nvme_iops_p90 > baseline by 4x for 2m. affected: 14 nodes.

mike: possible coupling between janitor concurrency and scratch GC? if cleaner spawns many tiny writers/deletes we hit write amplification and queue depth collapse.

jamal: agree. also see increased write latency from kernel which pushes NVMe controller to drop requests -> opaque errors. firmware retry storms amplify latency.

elaine: short mitigation: throttle cleaner to 8 workers per host and bump its backoff jitter. can we flip that via config template?

oncall-maya: oncall play: set cleaner concurrency to 8 in us-west1 via feature-flag and schedule a rolling restart of cleaner pods. I'll take it.

sara: doing a dry run on canary pool (gnode-uw1-[040-046]) now. early numbers look better: %util down to ~60 and errors stop for the last 30s.

mike: nice. long term: add IO cgroup limits on janitor and consider dynamic shaping based on nvme queue depth. also we should surface the opaque error counts in Console as a regression metric.

jamal: +1 on visibility. also let's capture a per-node SMART snapshot and map to provisioning events so we can proactively retire drives before they become crash points.

elaine: action items: (1) throttle cleaner concurrency in us-west1 (inflight) (2) collect SMART snapshots for 20 affected nodes (jamal) (3) add opaque error metric to Console (mike) (4) create runbook addendum for opaque nvme timeouts (sara)

oncall-maya: i've applied the FF to canary and scheduled rollouts to remainder over 30m window. monitoring now.

sara: can confirm canary improved GPU attach success rate from 94% -> 99% during the test window.

mike: cost note — if we keep very conservative retire policy we might spin up more preemptible replacements; quantify risk vs replacement cost. tagging finance later.

jamal: i'll run smartctl --all on affected nodes and post results to the incident doc. quick sample:```
smartctl 7.2 2020-12-30 
Device Model: ACME NVMe 980X
Reallocated_Sector_Ct: 35 (prefail)
Media_Wearout_Indicator: 12
```

elaine: thanks. once rollouts finish we'll keep the FF for 24h and re-evaluate. if errors reappear we escalate to firmware vendor for a deeper loop.

sara: closing the thread for now — will re-open if opaque errors recur. thanks all :thumbsup:
